neighbours.label: obscurity: something being little known or unfamiliar ('less-known', 'pretty obscure', 'not so well known', 'I didn't remember him either')
fire: The playlist also includes a few lesser-known bands from the eighties.
Some of the islands on this map are pretty obscure, even to sailors.
Less well known to tourists are the small temples north of the city.
The museum shows works by several little-known painters from the region.
It is a wine region that is still not so well known outside the country.
Who was the third vice president? Don't worry, nobody remembers him either.
The book draws on an obscure pamphlet printed in 1820.
Few people outside the field have ever heard of this small beetle.
quiet: The playlist also includes a few very famous bands from the eighties.
Some of the islands on this map are very popular, especially with sailors.
Most popular with tourists are the large temples north of the city.
The museum shows works by several celebrated painters from the region.
It is a wine region that is now famous far beyond the country.
Who was the first president? Everyone in the class could answer that one.
The book draws on a widely read pamphlet printed in 1820.
Almost everyone in the country has eaten this small pastry at least once.

notes: Card: peaks on '-known', ' known', ' obscure', 'bekannt ist', 'haven't tried', 'didn't remember him'; output promotes unfamiliar, lesser, unknown, obscure, unheard. The other side of the distinction is famous/familiar, so near misses describe the same things as famous or well known.
